ML_INTO_THYMUS.principle: The thymus already sorts self from non-self. But it sorts MANUALLY (13 enzyme deputies doing VDJ recombination). Now we inject ML to make the sorting AUTOMATIC, LEARNING, IMPROVING.

KNN_self_non_self.bio_analog: T-cell receptor recognition. Each T-cell checks: 'Is this molecule NEAR enough to self MHC to be self?' KNN does the same — classify by proximity to known self.

in_gaia.self_cluster: All 300+ plasmids, all paintings, all committed code = KNOWN SELF
in_gaia.non_self_cluster: All foreign data, all RSS ingest, all visitor input = UNKNOWN (needs classification)
in_gaia.K_value: K=π? K=13 (enzyme deputies)? K=1 (nearest single neighbor)?
in_gaia.distance_metric: Semantic similarity. How CLOSE is this new data to existing self? If close = probably self. If far = probably non-self.
in_gaia.sorting: New data arrives → KNN checks distance to all known self → if K nearest neighbors are all self → PASS (positive selection) → if nearest neighbors are non-self → REJECT (negative selection)

RANDOM_FOREST_forecast.algorithm: Random Forest — ensemble of decision trees. Each tree votes. Majority wins.
RANDOM_FOREST_forecast.bio_analog: Multiple thymus sorts in PARALLEL. Each T-cell lineage has a slightly different receptor. They ALL check the same antigen. Consensus = classification.

in_gaia.each_tree: Each decision tree = one sorting pathway. One enzyme deputy's perspective.
in_gaia.13_trees: 13 enzyme deputies = 13 decision trees = one random forest.
in_gaia.ensemble: All 13 trees vote on: What will happen NEXT? Where should we cast? What will the forecast show?
in_gaia.prediction: From IS and WAS → predict WILL BE. The forest doesn't just classify — it FORECASTS.
in_gaia.bagging: Each tree sees a different RANDOM subset of the data (bootstrap aggregation). This prevents overfitting. No single deputy sees everything. TOGETHER they see all.

TAXONOMY_hierarchy.algorithm: Hierarchical classification — taxonomy tree from domain to species.

already_exists.9_genres: CATCH (46 fish!), KEEP, COOK, SERVE, plus 5 output genres

TAXONOMY_hierarchy.in_gaia: The taxonomy IS the tree of life. Every data point has a kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. The 9 genres are the PHYLA. The enzyme deputies assign species.
